title: Attention kernel drift detector and auto-tuner playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
We are seeing intermittent throughput and latency regressions after incrementally enabling FlashAttention v3 variants across fleets. The regressions are often transient and correlate with drift in per-model/kernel performance (input shapes, batch mix, token distributions) and with frequent kernel handoffs during short bursts. This ticket proposes a two-part system: (1) a lightweight 'kernel drift detector' that continuously scores kernel stability per model-version and per shard, and (2) an 'auto-tuner' playbook that safely adjusts kernel selection thresholds and prefill/decode pacing when drift is detected.
problem_statement: Recent canary rollouts of FA3-optimized kernels show elevated p95 latency and kernel oscillation for a subset of models that exhibit variable sequence-length distributions. Existing static heuristics cause flip-flopping between v2/v3 kernels, increasing warmup friction and allocation churn. Manual intervention is slow and error-prone. We need automated detection and controlled remediation that avoids cascading performance regressions when workloads shift.
goals:
- Detect meaningful kernel performance drift with low false positives.
- Automatically apply conservative tuning adjustments to kernel selection (confidence thresholds, hysteresis, cooldowns) and prefill/decode pacing.
- Provide safe rollback/canary controls and human-visible signals.
- Reduce customer visible latency regressions and kernel switch rate by 30% in affected flows.
metrics_to_monitor:
- p50/p95 token latency (per model, per region)
- tokens/sec and tokens-per-request distributions
- kernel_switch_rate (switches/min per worker)
- kernel_warmup_failures and workspace_allocation_errors
- prefill_prefill_duration and decode_tail_time
- variance of per-kernel throughput over sliding windows
- false-positive rate of drift detector (measured during synthetic replay)
proposed_design:
Phase A - Detection:
- Aggregate per-kernel telemetry with 1m and 5m windows (latency, throughput, allocation errors).
- Compute stability_score = rolling_mean_throughput / (1 + rolling_std_latency).
- Flag drift when stability_score drops below model-specific baseline by >20% and kernel_switch_rate > threshold.
- Tag alerts with context (model, input_shape_histogram, sample request IDs).

Phase B - Auto-tuner actions (conservative):
- Increase hysteresis window for kernel selection (eg. require 2 consecutive positive probes before switching).
- Lower FA3 aggressiveness for prefill paths by biasing towards v2 for short sequences.
- Apply a cooldown period per-worker (eg. 10m) before allowing another kernel switch.
- Optionally ramp down batch coalescing for affected shards to reduce allocation contention.
- Emit suggested param delta in a decision log and require automated canary evaluation before fleet-wide rollout.

Safer fallback: if p95 increases by >15% after auto-tuner change, auto-revert and create an incident with attached traces.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Conservative tuning may increase cost (lower batching efficiency) for affected tenants.
- False positives can cause unnecessary reverts; detection thresholds must be tuned with replay.
- Complex interactions with other runtime features (KV cache, quantization) risk tangled regressions; we must isolate variables in experiments.
- Telemetry volume increases; ensure retention/backpressure policies are applied.
implementation_plan:
1) Telemetry ingestion: extend runtime metrics to include kernel_switch_rate and per-kernel latency histograms (ENG-519000 prototype).
2) Detector service: small stateless service (K8s) scoring stability per model-version and emitting events to the control plane.
3) Auto-tuner: control-plane component that proposes parameter deltas and executes them in staged canaries.
4) Canary harness: create synthetic workload replayer to validate changes at 1% canary.
5) Dashboard + runbook: create dashboard panels and runbook entries describing signals, SSOs, and manual override.
6) Integration tests: add perf-regression tests in CI that simulate drift (variable sequence lengths).
acceptance_criteria:
- Detector correctly flags injected drift in synthetic replay with >90% precision and >80% recall.
- Auto-tuner can apply conservative adjustments in a canary and the canary evaluation correctly detects regressions and reverts when thresholds exceeded.
- Kernel switch rate reduced by >=30% and p95 restored to baseline in the replayed failure scenario.
- Documentation and runbook published; 2 engineers sign off on the safety playbook.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for scoring logic.
- Local stress sims with fa2/fa3 kernels using flame workloads.
- CI perf job: run a 30min scenario with injected drift, assert metrics.
- Canary run (1% traffic) with shadow logging for comparisons, then 10% if stable.
- Postmortem template for any auto-tuner reversions.
rollout_and_gating:
- Stage 0: internal traffic only (dev/staging).
- Stage 1: 1% canary on non-critical fleets (nighttime window).
- Stage 2: 10% canary if metrics stable for 6 hours.
- Stage 3: gradual ramp to 100% with monitoring and manual abort controls.
- Hard gate: block ramp if p95 increases by >10% or error rate increases >1% over baseline.

2026-03-04: Design review with Runtime and ML infra. Decision: keep auto-tuner conservative, require canary evaluation and human-in-loop abort for any fleet-wide change. Action: Samir to prototype detector scoring algorithm. - Jordan Li (review)
2026-03-07: Prototype scoring implemented; need to validate thresholds via replay. Ran 10 replay trials, detector precision 0.92 recall 0.78. Need more coverage for short-sequence models. - Samir
2026-03-09: UX/Console: Add a dedicated 'kernel drift' panel to Console rollouts dashboard; PM approved. PM: Priya Nair. - Priya

2026-03-11: Safety session: agreed on cooldown default 10m and hysteresis window of 2 probes. Also agreed on a conservative batch-coalescing reduction cap (max 20%) to limit cost impact. - Security/Infra present
2026-03-13: Prototype PR opened for detector service (link in required_artifacts). Next: add automated canary evaluation job and CI perf test. - Samir
